# Imaging-based In Situ Spatial Transcriptomics Tools

A curated, automatically updated list of software for **imaging-based (in situ) spatial transcriptomics**: 10x Genomics Xenium, Bruker/NanoString CosMx, Vizgen MERSCOPE and MERFISH, seqFISH, STARmap, in situ sequencing (ISS), Resolve Molecular Cartography and smFISH-based methods. Tools are grouped by analysis step. Sequencing-based methods (Visium, Stereo-seq, Slide-seq) are out of scope unless a tool also handles imaging-based data.

![tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-133-2b7bb9) ![awaiting review](https://img.shields.io/badge/awaiting%20review-0-e0a100) [![weekly discovery](https://github.com/amnahsiddiqa/imaging-spatial-tx-tools/actions/workflows/weekly-discovery.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/amnahsiddiqa/imaging-spatial-tx-tools/actions/workflows/weekly-discovery.yml)

Every Monday a GitHub Action searches GitHub and Europe PMC (PubMed + bioRxiv/medRxiv) for new tools and opens a pull request with the hits for review ([how it works](#how-this-list-is-maintained)).

**Related lists:** [Spatial_transcriptomics_tools](https://github.com/p-gueguen/Spatial_transcriptomics_tools) (all spatial technologies; this list's model) · [awesome_spatial_omics](https://github.com/crazyhottommy/awesome_spatial_omics)

**Legend:** Platforms = imaging technologies named in the repo README or paper abstract (detected automatically; blank = none named) · ★ = GitHub stars · 🗄️ archived by its owner · 💤 no commits for 2+ years

## How this list is maintained

- **Source of truth:** [`data/tools.yaml`](data/tools.yaml). This README is generated from it by [`scripts/build_readme.py`](scripts/build_readme.py); edits made here directly are overwritten.
- **Weekly discovery** ([`scripts/discover.py`](scripts/discover.py), run by [`weekly-discovery.yml`](.github/workflows/weekly-discovery.yml)):
  - Europe PMC: papers and preprints from the last 21 days whose abstract mentions an imaging-based platform and whose title or abstract reads as a method, tool, benchmark or resource. Code links are taken from the abstract, or from a GitHub repo named after the tool. This is how brand-new tools are usually found.
  - GitHub: repositories with at least 10 stars that mention an imaging-based platform (Xenium, CosMx, MERFISH, seqFISH, STARmap, ISS, …) in their name, description, topics or README and are not in the list yet. Each is scored on simple tool-likeness signals (install instructions, licence, description, stars, linked paper; minus points for one-off analysis repos) and kept above a fixed score. New 0-star repos are skipped on purpose: almost all are personal analyses.
  - Hits are sorted into categories by keyword rules in [`config/search.yaml`](config/search.yaml) and added with `status: candidate`. Stars, last commit and archived status of listed tools are refreshed in the same run.
  - If anything changed, the Action opens (or adds to) one pull request, `auto/weekly-candidates`, for a human to review. Nothing reaches the main list without that review.
- **Papers** linked from a repo are the first DOI in its README that resolves in Crossref or DataCite; preprints are labelled *Preprint*.
- **Limits:** keyword search misses tools that never name a platform, classification is approximate, and the paper link can occasionally be a related paper rather than the tool's own. Corrections are welcome via [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

*Last list change: 2026-11-03.*
